pages.wrong_reason: GMW87 build semi-honest two-party computation from oblivious transfer (obtained there from trapdoor permutations); commitments and zero-knowledge proofs enter GMW87 only in the compiler from semi-honest to malicious security. 'COM is complete for two-party computation in the semi-honest model' is therefore not a theorem of GMW87, and is believed false: commitments exist given any one-way function (Naor91 + HILL99), so the claim would yield OT from OWFs, which no relativizing reduction can (IR89). Ideal commitment is also trivially realizable against semi-honest parties, so it cannot be an information-theoretically complete functionality there. The page's SUSPECTED note and .reductions/suspected-errors.json (entries red-cs-to-smpc-gmw87, red-cs-to-tpc-gmw87, same underlying prose) record the same error. The defensible edges already exist: OT => MPC (red-ot-to-mpc-kil88) and GC + OT => 2PC (red-gc-and-ot-to-two-party-computation-2pc); the correct COM edge is the compiler (COM + ZK lift semi-honest security to malicious security), a different conclusion object.

pages.statement: A verifiable secret sharing scheme is a [[secret-sharing|secret sharing]] scheme whose dealer also publishes [[commitment-scheme|commitments]] to the shares (or to the coefficients of the sharing polynomial) together with a consistency check — the commitments' homomorphism or a zero-knowledge proof — so that each party can verify that the committed shares determine a single secret, even when the dealer is malicious.
notes_to_keep: 'verifiable-secret-sharing' has no page of its own.
flags: Migrated text is a definitional gloss of VSS, not a theorem; the hyperedge 'generic COM + generic SS => VSS' has no canonical citation (researcher tried vendor/cryptobib and web search; verifier could not reach Springer/IACR/ACM full texts either). The Statement is kept as a definition with no citation marker.

Commitments to shares alone do not give a consistency check: a party can verify its own opening but not that all committed shares lie on one degree-t polynomial. The attributable constructions use HOMOMORPHIC commitments (Feldman, FOCS 1987; Pedersen, CRYPTO 1991) on Shamir sharing; VSS itself is due to Chor-Goldwasser-Micali-Awerbuch (FOCS 1985). A generic route (commit to shares, prove consistency in zero knowledge, given broadcast) also needs ZK from COM and interaction, and no source states it in this generic form.
Consider re-scoping the page to Feldman/Pedersen VSS with a homomorphic-commitment hypothesis, which would make it sourceable.
verifier_changes: statement: made precise that plain commitments to shares need a consistency check (homomorphism or ZK proof) — the researcher's wording implied commitments alone let parties verify consistency
flags consolidated; disposition undetermined and status stub approved

pages.wrong_reason: coNP ⊆ AM is open, not a theorem: it would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to the second level (Boppana-Hastad-Zachos, 'Does co-NP have short interactive proofs?', Inf. Process. Lett. 25(2):127-132, 1987). GS86 prove the private-coin/public-coin equivalence — every k-round private-coin interactive proof is simulated by a (k+2)-round Arthur-Merlin protocol — and give no AM protocol for coNP. The bullet at content/Complexity/co-nondeterministic-polynomial-time.md:21 attaches GS86 to a statement the paper does not make, as the page's SUSPECTED note records, and contradicts the collapse argument in co-arthur-merlin.md. Correct neighbouring edges exist: coNP ⊆ coAM (red-conp-to-coam, from NP ⊆ AM by complementation) and coNP ⊆ PSPACE (red-conp-to-pspace); coNP ⊆ IP (LFKN/Shamir) would be a separate sourced page.

pages.statement: Any non-trivial single-server [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|PIR]] — one whose total communication is strictly less than the $n$-bit database — implies [[oblivious-transfer|OT]]; if the PIR has communication $c(n)$, the OT has communication $c(n) \cdot \poly(\secpar)$ [[DMO00 - Single Database Private Information Retrieval Implies Oblivious Transfer|DMO00]]. In particular, non-trivial single-server PIR is complete for secure two-party and multi-party computation [[DMO00 - Single Database Private Information Retrieval Implies Oblivious Transfer|DMO00]].
notes_to_keep: 'Non-trivial' (total communication strictly less than the $n$-bit database) is a load-bearing qualifier on the hypothesis that the flat slug `cpir` loses; it is preserved in the Statement.

pages.wrong_reason: As recorded the edge asserts an unconditional equivalence CZK = IP, but on the source page (computational-zero-knowledge.md:29) the equality is a sub-bullet under 'Assuming OWFs exist'; the migration dropped the hypothesis, as the page's own Notes record. BGG+90 prove IP ⊆ CZK assuming a secure bit commitment (hence any one-way function, via Naor91 + HILL99); unconditionally only the trivial direction CZK ⊆ IP holds. Unconditional CZK = IP is not known and cannot currently be proved, since one-way functions are necessary for non-trivial CZK (Ostrovsky-Wigderson, ISTCS 1993; the SZK/hard-on-average case is Ost91). Correct replacement edges: (i) a conditional edge with hypotheses {hash-function (OWF), ip} and conclusion czk, sourced to BGG+90 (cf. red-hash-function-to-czk, which records the GMW91 'OWF => NP ⊆ CZK' analogue), and (ii) the trivial unconditional inclusion CZK ⊆ IP as a folklore page.

sources.ref_file_title: DJ01 - A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System
sources.note: cryptobib key PKC:DamJur01: author 'Ivan Damgård and Mats Jurik', pages 119-136, year 2001, doi 10.1007/3-540-44586-2_9, all verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib; existence of the PKC 2001 paper and of the BRICS RS-00-45 report confirmed by web search (publisher/DBLP pages are egress-blocked). Keep the spelling 'Mats Jurik' so npm run sync-cryptobib passes. No existing reference file with key DJ01.

pages.class_justification: DJ01 make no black-box-notion claim, and the hypothesis is a hardness assumption rather than a primitive, so the RTV04 axes do not apply; the honest value is unstated.
pages.statement: Under [[decisional-composite-residuosity#d-th-composite-residuosity|$d$-th composite residuosity]] — hardness of distinguishing $n^d$-th residues modulo $n^{d+1}$ from uniform — the Damgård–Jurik cryptosystem is an IND-CPA-secure additively [[homomorphic-encryption|homomorphic encryption]] scheme: for an RSA modulus $n$, $\Enc(\pk, m; r) = (1+n)^m \cdot r^{n^d} \bmod n^{d+1}$ encrypts $m \in \ZZ_{n^d}$, the product of two ciphertexts encrypts $m_1 + m_2 \bmod n^d$, and $d = 1$ is Paillier [[DJ01 - A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System|DJ01]]. For every $d$ the $d$-th assumption is equivalent to [[decisional-composite-residuosity|DCR]], so the message space grows with $d$ under the same assumption [[DJ01 - A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System|DJ01]].
pages.sketch: Ciphertexts multiply to add plaintexts, so $\Eval$ for addition is multiplication modulo $n^{d+1}$. Decryption raises the ciphertext to a secret exponent that is $0 \bmod \lambda$ and $1 \bmod n^d$, with $\lambda = \mathrm{lcm}(p-1, q-1)$; this kills the $r^{n^d}$ component and leaves $(1+n)^m$, from which $m$ is read off digit by digit modulo $n, n^2, \ldots, n^d$ using the binomial expansion of $(1+n)^m$.
notes_to_keep: d-th-composite-residuosity has no page of its own (section of decisional-composite-residuosity).
flags: Conclusion `he` is coarser than what is proved: the scheme is an additively (partially) homomorphic PKE, not general HE — consider conclusion additively-homomorphic-encryption to match red-dcr-to-partially-homomorphic-encryption-phe-pai99.

DJ01 prove the degree-$d$ assumption equivalent to base DCR, resolving the migration note 'the relation between the d-th variant and base DCR is never stated'; the edge could equivalently be recorded with hypothesis dcr.

sources.ref_file_title: DJ01 - A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System
sources.note: cryptobib key PKC:DamJur01 (author 'Ivan Damgård and Mats Jurik', pages 119-136, doi 10.1007/3-540-44586-2_9 verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib); same reference page as proposed for red-d-th-composite-residuosity-to-he.

pages.class_justification: Pai99 makes no black-box-notion claim, and the hypothesis is a hardness assumption rather than a primitive, so the RTV04 axes do not apply; the honest value is unstated.
pages.statement: Under [[decisional-composite-residuosity|DCR]], the Paillier cryptosystem is an IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]] that is additively homomorphic: for an RSA modulus $n$ and $g \in \ZZ_{n^2}^*$ of order divisible by $n$ (e.g. $g = n+1$), $\Enc(\pk, m; r) = g^m \cdot r^n \bmod n^2$ with $m \in \ZZ_n$ and $r \getsr \ZZ_n^*$, and $\Enc(\pk, m_1; r_1) \cdot \Enc(\pk, m_2; r_2) \bmod n^2$ encrypts $m_1 + m_2 \bmod n$ [[Pai99 - Public-key cryptosystems based on composite degree residuosity classes|Pai99]]. Semantic security of the scheme is equivalent to DCR [[Pai99 - Public-key cryptosystems based on composite degree residuosity classes|Pai99]].
pages.sketch: An encryption of $m$ is $g^m$ times a random $n$-th residue, so a DCR challenge $z$ embeds as $c^* = g^{m_b} \cdot z \bmod n^2$: if $z$ is an $n$-th residue, $c^*$ is a fresh encryption of $m_b$; if $z$ is uniform, $c^*$ is independent of $b$. The reduction runs the IND-CPA adversary once.
pages.security_loss: Tight: one call to the IND-CPA adversary; semantic security is equivalent to DCR.
pages.improvements_text: - The Damgård–Jurik generalization works modulo $n^{d+1}$ with message space $\ZZ_{n^d}$ for any $d \ge 1$, remains additively homomorphic, and is semantically secure under the same DCR assumption — [[DJ01 - A Generalisation, a Simplification and Some Applications of Paillier's Probabilistic Public-Key System|DJ01]]

pages.class_justification: Folklore construction; the hypothesis is an assumption rather than a primitive, so the RTV04 axes do not apply, and no source states a class.
pages.statement: [[decisional-composite-residuosity|DCR]] implies a non-interactive [[commitment-scheme|commitment scheme]] of either flavour, both instances of Paillier encryption with the public key as commitment key. Perfectly binding, computationally hiding: commit to $m \in \ZZ_n$ as $c = (1+n)^m \cdot r^n \bmod n^2$ with $r \getsr \ZZ_n^*$ and open by revealing $(m, r)$; for a well-formed RSA modulus $n$ the map $(m, r) \mapsto c$ is a bijection $\ZZ_n \times \ZZ_n^* \to \ZZ_{n^2}^*$, so binding is perfect, and hiding is IND-CPA security of Paillier under DCR. Perfectly hiding, computationally binding: with a commitment key $K$ that is a random $n$-th residue (a CRS, or receiver-generated with a proof of residuosity), $c = K^m \cdot r^n \bmod n^2$ is a uniform $n$-th residue independent of $m$, and a committer who opens $c$ two ways distinguishes $K$ from a uniform key, under which binding is perfect; binding is therefore computational under DCR — folklore.
pages.sketch: Both are Paillier encryption under the commitment key: with $g = 1+n$ of order $n$ the map is injective (perfect binding) and hiding is IND-CPA; with $g$ an $n$-th residue the commitment is a uniform residue (perfect hiding), and DCR-indistinguishability of the two key types makes binding computational.
notes_to_keep: Commitment flavour is not part of the conclusion identifier.
flags: The migrated flavour (statistically hiding, computationally binding) IS achievable from DCR via the residue-key Paillier commitment now in the Statement, so decisional-composite-residuosity.md:33 is not wrong; the researcher's 'flavours swapped' flag is withdrawn. The immediate construction (Paillier as commitment) is perfectly binding instead; both flavours are stated. Suspected-errors entry red-dcr-to-cs (severity low) can be closed with the source bullet amended to name both flavours.

Hiding-mode key must be an $n$-th residue: a receiver who chooses a non-residue key and knows the factorization of $n$ decrypts. Hence a CRS or a proof of residuosity; `model` stays `standard` for the perfectly-binding construction, in which the committer generates $n$.

Binding of the perfectly-binding flavour against a malicious committer needs $n$ well-formed (injectivity uses $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$); receiver-side checks or a well-formedness proof are required.

Attributable form of the hiding-mode construction: Damgård–Nielsen, 'Perfect Hiding and Perfect Binding Universally Composable Commitment Schemes with Constant Expansion Factor', CRYPTO 2002 (eprint 2001/091, BRICS RS-01-41; existence verified by web search) — Paillier-based mixed commitments with perfectly hiding and perfectly binding key modes. Not added as a source: the page's claim is the flavour-agnostic folklore one; add if a citation is wanted.

The migration note attributing statistically hiding DCR commitments to Damgard-Fujisaki is imprecise: DF02-style integer commitments live in hidden-order groups under strong-RSA/factoring-type assumptions, not DCR; the note was not kept.
